correctness.rationale: Clearing denominators is reversible on b,u>0. The exact cubic discriminant factors through D(b). Sturm theory gives three simple positive roots of D and one negative root, with rational isolating intervals. Sign analysis proves the cubic has one positive root when its discriminant is negative and three positive roots when positive; b=1 is handled by direct factorization. A nonzero exact resultant excludes triple roots at the three endpoints, yielding exactly two distinct positive roots there. The proof is global in b>0; decimal evaluations are not used as proof.
